text_fidelity_a: Roku 3 Streaming Media Player (2014 model) Without repeating what everyone has said here, I will speak for Roku's support of the Plex media streaming software which is a free Roku channel. If you have never heard of it, it is a fantastic solution that allows you to use Roku (as well as all your portable devices and remote computers, including ones on the internet-at-large) to stream all of the movies on your computer, regardless of the format. On Roku, you can browse the movie collection on your computer using a slick interface and watch it in full resolution. (This is only if you have a fast connection like a home wireless network, and you need to configure it to do this- an easy settings change.) If your computer can play it, so can your Roku. The key to this is because all the transcoding of the video file happens on your computer so all Roku has to do is play the video stream. The result is that you can easily fast-forward and rewind, as well and have the jump-back feature like the TiVo has. This was the primary reason that I bought the Roku as it is a lot easier to use than trying to connect your computer directly to your TV and muddling about with computer controls to watch movies. The Plex interface on Roku is easy to use and very slick. It does nice things like look up movie data so you have the cover art, theme music, and movie info for you to peruse as you are browsing your library. Finally, there is the "Plex it!" feature which you can use with your computer's browser, so that when you find a video on the internet on your computer, you want to queue it up for later to watch on your TV, and it will appear in your movie queue in Plex on Roku, regardless of the video format! This also gets around the one annoying thing about Roku and that it doesn't have a native YouTube channel for some reason.
text_fidelity_b: Roku 3 Streaming Media Player (2014 model)

The Echo itself seems great and does what it's supposed to do. My huge concern is who can drop in on my echo. Here's why I say this. My ex has an Alexa device and had full control over it while living here. I never had access to that account besides being able to talk to the Alexa. When I set this Echo up in my house all of a sudden his Alexa popped up under the communications tab. I don't have this person's number in my phone and I don't show any devices when I go into my Amazon account besides my new Echo. I can't find any option at all to block this person or get this person off my Echo. From what it looks like they can just drop in whenever they want which they had a bad habit of doing on their device when it was here. I find no way to remove that device without turning off the "drop-in" feature which is why I bought it so I can connect with my son if I'm not here. If there was a way to get this persons information off my Echo it would be a 5 star review, but since I have to worry everyday if they will just be able to drop in and be watching us or we won't know they are dropping in that's a huge thing for me. So if someone knows how to get them off it would be great if someone could tell me how that works. Otherwise, this rating will stay the same as I don't like not knowing if someone will be able to spy on us.

text_fidelity_a:
Synsen Replacement Ear Pads Cushion Compatible for Bose QuietComfort QC2,QuietComfort 15 QC15,QuietComfort QC25,QuietComfort 35 QC35,Bose AE2,AE2i,AE2w,SoundTrue, SoundLink (Around-Ear) Headphones I purchased these replacement pads for my Bose QC-15 headphones as the old pads were torn and needed to be replaced. I selected this set of pads based on the positive reviews here on Amazon with the thought that they would be the same as the original pads. While they look the same, they are indeed slightly different.

First things first - these pads are fairly easy to install though they do require a little persistence to get them to snap into place. The earphones themselves have small tabs around the edges designed to snap the pads' bases into place and hold securely, and if the pads are not snapped down they simply will not stay securely. The inner foam and cloth shield that covers the electronics is easy to install but I had trouble with the double-sided tape that holds them in place - the adhesive did not want to release the cover strip and I had real difficulty peeling that strip away without ripping the actual cloth.

Once in place, the phones look exactly like they did when they were new, but I found three differences. First, the phones no longer fit into the case as easily as they once did. Instead of just turning the cups to lay flat and simply putting them in the case, now I have to mess with them slightly to fit into the case properly, though they can be made to fit. More noticeable, though, is that the pads are not as effective as the originals for passive noise canceling. A fan that I have in my office used to be canceled out almost completely with the combination of passive and active noise canceling but is now more audible than when the original pads were in place. I would not say the difference is enough to render the earphones' ability to cancel noise completely compromised, but they are definitely not the same. Finally, these replacement pads are just a little less supple and soft than the original pads. It is not all that noticeable until comparing the original and replacement pads side by side. You have to really be looking closely for the difference to notice it, but it's there.

The difference in noise canceling ability is most noticeable when working in an environment with reverb. I use my phones to monitor sound coming through a professional sound board because these have always done an excellent job of eliminating reverb and leaving just what comes through the sound board. With these new pads in place, I can now hear a lot of reverb, even when I press the phones tight over my ears and have ensured that they completely cover my ears so it's not a gapping issue. The material is different, plain and simple.

These are not bad replacement pads by any means. They are very good, they are comfortable and they do make these phones look brand new again. That said, they were not manufactured by Bose and there are some differences. When considering the cost difference between these and Bose parts, the trade-offs balance out favorably. If you have to have an exact match with the original pads, these are very close but not 100% identical. If you are satisfied with a [roughly] 90%-95% match, these pads work nicely for a lot less than original manufacturer pads.
text_fidelity_b: Synsen Replacement Ear Pads Cushion Compatible for Bose QuietComfort QC2,QuietComfort 15 QC15,QuietComfort QC25,QuietComfort 35 QC35,Bose AE2,AE2i,AE2w,SoundTrue, SoundLink (Around-Ear) Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
UGREEN Lightning to USB Cable Data Syncing Charging Cord Compatible for iPhone 7,7plus,6S,6 Plus,iPhone5s,5c,5,iPad Mini,Mini 2,Air Etc MFI Certified (5ft, Silver) I have only recently started using UGREEN cables and so far every one of their cables I have used has been a top-notch product. I was interested to see how well their lightning cable would work out for me and, based on my experiences with their other cables I expected this cable to be excellent. I have not been disappointed.

First things first – this is an Apple-certified cable which is not insignificant. Because it is certified it will work right with your Apple device and the device will not complain about it being an unrecognized cable. If you have used cheaper cables that do not come with a certification you have seen the warning messages that appear when you connect it. This one will not cause that problem which is good right out of the box.

This cable seems to be well made and so far I have found no issues with build quality or assembly. The insulation is nice and thick and it securely attached on both ends so it will not pull away from the plugs. Each plug is shielded in an aluminum sheath which protects the plug and makes it a little easier to grip. I have the 5’ version of this cable which is nice; I like that I have a little more leeway with the extra length of the cable.

There’s something I want to emphasize about this cable which many might not consider or may think is insignificant. UGREEN has put their name right on the plug ends, where it is easy to see and read. This says that they believe in this product enough to brand it, which is actually uncommon. Most of the cables on my desk are not branded so it is very nice being able to identify a cable by manufacturer. When one goes bad, if it is not branded it is difficult to know where that cable came from. The very best micro USB cable I own is by UGREEN and because it is branded it is very easy for me to identify in the tangle on my desk. Now I can tell which lightning cable is theirs too.

I have not had this cable long enough to see how well it will hold up over time but in the time I have had it, it has been reliable and compatible. I like the extra length too which gives me some flexibility when figuring out where to put it and the device I connect to it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: UGREEN Lightning to USB Cable Data Syncing Charging Cord Compatible for iPhone 7,7plus,6S,6 Plus,iPhone5s,5c,5,iPad Mini,Mini 2,Air Etc MFI Certified (5ft, Silver)

I normally buy regular over the head earphones, and got these because of their noise cancelling properties and because they looked like they would be more comfortable. Our neighbors have a dog that barks all day long (literally) when they leave their home and I wanted peace and quiet when I go outside now that it is warming up and gardening season is here. Like I said, the noise cancelling works great. But, it only works as long as they stay in my ears, so I am using my husbands Bose OE2 headphones instead.

If my ears would hold the buds, I would LOVE these. They do work as promised. I am just disappointed there is no such thing as an over the ear clip accessory for those of us with ears that don't do well with them.

I called Bose and they are sending me another set of eartips to see if maybe these were just missized or defective.

text_fidelity_a:
eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert Purchased two of these Eufy 2K cams to test out and determine if they're good enough to replace the Wyze cams. These Eufy cams definitely capture higher resolution, more detailed videos compared to the Wyze cam v2. The pan and tilt feature is great when I want to remotely check different parts of an area and the pan/tilt action is very silent. You can set the cam to automatically track/follow motion when it's detected. The amount of time it takes to go to live view on a cam is within a couple of seconds and the alerts for motion is definitely faster than the Wyze cam v2. The time from me waving my hand in front of the cam and getting an alert on my phone is about 3 seconds or less.

I did experience issues with one Eufy cam where it would randomly start panning by itself and would do a 360 degree pan. The Eufy app works overall, but I did notice several times I had connection issues when trying to live view, but this issue also happens on Wyze cams, too.

You can set the Eufy cam to record only when motion or sound is detected or set the cam to continuous recording. If you choose continuous recording the video resolution will be reduced to 1080p resolution. For motion recording you can set up activity zones (specific areas you want to detect motion), adjust motion detection sensitivity, detect people, detect pets, and detect all other motion. Eufy's app is still missing the ability to view multiple live views of cams at the same time, which is a shame and hopefully they have a software update for that.

Overall, the Eufy 2k cam has great video quality, the pan/tilt motion is useful and silent, has a lot of features, and the price is competitive. They go on sale from time to time, so if you're not in a hurry then I'd wait for a sale.
text_fidelity_b: eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert

text_fidelity_a:
Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Once calibrated, this PC tablet works wonderfully. It is responsive to the stowable stylus or a tap of my fingernail, and I can even scroll with my thumb after adjusting the right edge width. The screen is sharp and clear, and it's speedy enough for pleasurable surfing and blog-reading, which is what I mostly want to use it for. I have not watched any HD movies on it yet, although the sample movie clip included with the computer shows what it's capable of...and it's gorgeous.

But I have a problem with the Archos 9. Because there is no fan, which makes for a very quiet experience, the lithium battery does get hot when held in your hands. Now, maybe there are people who will use this computer by pulling out the little easel-like stick in the back, but not me. I want to curl up on the sofa with it like a book. So I could see immediately that I wanted to rotate my Archos 9 PC Tablet's screen to portrait orientation so the battery would be at the top and not bother me so much. Well, doing so was a BIG mistake. Once you rotate the screen, it's pretty much impossible to recalibrate it; trying to move the cursor is like trying to walk without an inner ear: Directions ceased to make sense and I'd skew off East (or was it West?) when I meant to move North. It was all I could do to manage to restore the computer to its earlier state.

The little end piece of the easel-like appendage pulled off and I had to super-glue it back on, but that wasn't such a big deal. This appendage also stows into the back of the computer, and it can be pulled out short or long depending on whether you are watching a movie or trying to type on the on-screen keyboard. I can see it for watching a movie, but there's no way I'd ever try to type on the on-screen keyboard. Hunt-and-peck with the stylus is quicker. Needless to say, I will reach for my laptop if I have to do much typing.

I installed Skype, but it was too slow to show video unless I stopped everything else from running. This is fine with me, however, because I prefer to use Skype without the visuals. Google Chrome runs very well on it. I found I preferred the software keyboard (which you can drag around the screen) to the one that pops up when you press the keyboard key. I found that by keeping the former loaded and minimized to the tray, I can get around and do things online pretty efficiently. I just wish that battery didn't get so hot OR that I could easily/reliably rotate the screen to portrait. I gave this computer four stars because, on the whole, it's quite nice. But I must say that I am not likely to reach for the Archos 9 very often because of the discomfort from the battery heat when holding it in my hands. If they will come out with a software upgrade that will make screen rotation practical, then I will be a lot happier with this tablet PC.

A word to the wise: Immediately when you take your Archos 9 out of the box and get the software installed, you need to back it up. Don't wait a second longer than you have to. I was able to restore mine to its pristine newly installed state, but had I not backed it up, the whole thing would have been trashed by my little screen rotation exploit. You don't have a restore disk with this product. So be careful.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

Belkin N300 Wireless N Router (Latest Generation) (F9K1002) Bought this for my mother who has a small 2 bedroom apartment. Has been installed for over 3 weeks now. It was so very easy to install, simple instructions, did not have to adjust any settings. We just attached it to the DSL modem, loaded the CD into each computer that was going to use the network, followed the simple instructions, works great. We did have a problem trying to set up an account, which we still have not been able to do. May call later for assistance if we find it would be helpful to have an account, but so far everything works great.

We have had my mother's desktop computer (also running wireless now), her notebook computer, my notebook computer and the printer all running on the network at the same time. There was absolutely no degradation in service, have never had a problem with disconnects even with all computers running at the same time and two of the computers sending documents to the printer. This includes using one of the notebook computers at the furthest location in the apartment away from the router as possible. The only problem we have is the slower Verizon DSL service compared to the faster Verizon FIOS service I have at my house, so not a Belkin problem. Too bad my mother can't get FIOS. But her internet access is as fast as it was when it was attached directly to the modem.

Would highly recommend this product.

5/28/2015 - Just found this review I wrote in 2011. My mother is still using the same Belkin N150, still works great even if we have 3 computers running at the same time. The retirement community she lives in switched voice/Internet carriers about 6 months ago. Saw no difference in performance. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin N300 Wireless N Router (Latest Generation) (F9K1002)

text_fidelity_a: SanDisk 256GB Ultra Dual Drive USB Type-C - USB-C, USB 3.1 - SDDDC2-256G-G46 I bought this to back up my LG phone because I was forced to buy a new phone since LG no longer supports their phones and I was already starting to have issues with mine.  In buying a new phone, I was particularly freaked out about the possibility of losing my photos and other important files since the newer phones no longer have MicroSD cards for backup.  This seemed like a great option--along with backing up to Google and Amazon cloud services, it added another layer of protection.  The problem is that the C port didn't even fit into the C port on my phone--even though I took the case off my phone.  After essentially having to cram it in the port, I kept getting a warning that my data would be corrupted if I kept "ejecting" it.  It also wanted to back everything up to a MicroSD card, since it did not recognize that the SanDisk was even inserted into the phone.  Since I'd spent a considerable amount of time moving everything from my SD card to the internal memory of my phone in anticipation of having to transfer it to a new phone without a card slot, I most definitely didn't want to back up everything back onto my card, so I took the card out.  Even so, it still took quite some time for the phone to recognize the SanDisk, and finally start the back up.  From there, the process was fairly easy, BUT it should have never been so difficult to get the phone to recognize the SanDisk in the first place.  After the backup, I of course plugged the SanDisk into my laptop (without issues) and everything was indeed backed up.  It should NOT have been that difficult to plug the device into my phone however!  I will also mention, not that it's a big deal, but the device is considerably smaller than it looks to be on the Amazon website (less than .75x1.5").  At least I have an additional backup, but not as easily as I would have liked.  Given the issues I had with it I don't think I would purchase this particular device again.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk 256GB Ultra Dual Drive USB Type-C - USB-C, USB 3.1 - SDDDC2-256G-G46

Perixx Peripro-303MR Trackball, 1.34 Inch Replacement Ball for Perimice and M570, Matte Red I bought this replacement ball for my Logitech MX ERGO, which worked well for me before I accidentally dropped it and subsequently put a pock mark on the original ball. The ERGO still worked but would occasionally get stuck when the support pegs would catch the pock and cause the ball to resist - not enough to really hurt anything but just enough to make digital drawing difficult and just enough to annoy me. This replacement ball has taken care of that for me and has proven to be a worthwhile expense for me.

The ERGO and the M570 have the same size ball, so this ball can be used in either (I was using the ball from my old M570 in the ERGO while I waited for this ball to arrive). Replacement is a 30-second procedure and requires no special tools, though a pencil does make getting the old ball out a lot easier.

There are two different finish types available, glossy and matte. I chose the glossy in red. Operation has been absolutely smooth with no resistance at all and no catches. I haven’t noticed any operational differences between it and the original gray ball that came in my ERGO. And, in my opinion, the dark red of this ball actually looks a little nicer than the original silver ball as well as the blue M570 ball.

This wasn’t an expensive replacement and so far it has worked out very well for me. It has restored operation of my trackball to what it was before I damaged the original ball, which is really all I needed. Based on my experience with it, this is an easy replacement ball to recommend if you need to replace the ball in either a Logitech M570 or an MX ERGO.
text_fidelity_b: Perixx Peripro-303MR Trackball, 1.34 Inch Replacement Ball for Perimice and M570, Matte Red

text_fidelity_a:
NYNE Multimedia Inc Cruiser Portable Bluetooth Speaker (Grey/Green) Although there are a lot of positive points to be said about this product, a major flaw with it is that - even on low volumes and on songs without much bass - you can hear a bit of distortion, like crackly static, that sounds like a speaker that you're either working too hard or is at the end of its life. This becomes worse as the battery gets low. I consider this issue to be "understandable and sort of acceptable" considering the whole system has to run on battery power and most people aren't expecting high power out of such a setup. They might just have a high-pass crossover set too high to conserve power, and too much is cut off, resulting in messy sound.

When you charge your phone with the speaker's battery (which in itself is sort of a nice, if cannibalistic, feature, one that other devices claim even though it is inherent to the device; with this, the USB-A port was added specifically for this purpose), it lowers the volume to level 8 (there is nothing to tell you what level you're at) to keep from draining the battery quickly. Even at this medium level and below, this problem can be recognized.

The bike mounts are 4" apart, center to center, so make sure you have room on your bike handlebars if that is your purpose for ordering. Included bike mounts are good. It also comes with a neoprene case, a USB cable, and an audio cable, both red. With all these extras trying to give the appearance of premium, it doesn't actually come with a charger, not that this will be an issue for most people (you probably already have more than you know what to do with).

There should be keyhole slots built into the bike mounts so it could also be hung on the wall and removed easily, making it more versatile.

The unit pairs easily and immediately with my Blackberry every time, and it can control the tracks through the BT connection as well. It looks well made and has a good feel to it. It looks like it could almost be waterproof, although I noticed no mention or claim of that feature (so I'm sure it's not).

The sound overall isn't bad for a low voltage battery operated speaker, as long as you're not sitting down and listening too closely. I guess for the purposes of making noise as you ride around the neighborhood, it'll do just fine.

Retekess V111 Shortwave Radio, Portable Digital Radio Stereo Voice, Battery Operated with Favorite Key and Earphone Digital Alarm Clock for Hiking Walking When I was a kid 50 years ago, I asked for a SW radio for Christmas. We got our presents on Christmas Eve and when I took it up to my bedroom, I opened a storm window just enough to hang the extension wire out. I was able to listen to stations all over the world. Russia, England, Japan, India, etc. Didn't matter that I couldn't understand anything but English. These were voices from around the globe! I felt the world was in my hands. AM and FM, too. Big dial. Yes, the radio was big and bulky and forget any batteries. Power cord was it.

I bought this VITE just to see if SW would interest me still. I've only had it for a few hours, and it sure does. It's like my big, bulky radio was somehow shrunken down and forced into this tiny unit and with even more bells and whistles. Seems to be built very well and solid. Powered by 2 AAs. If you had a handheld transistor radio in the 60s, it's even smaller! Speaker is nothing to brag about, but so what? It's $20 bucks. Nice little SW. I might eventually look at something more powerful.

Lenovo Legion Y720 Gaming Laptop, 15.6" Full HD, Intel Core i7-7700HQ Processor, 16GB DDR4 RAM, 512GB SSD, GeForce GTX 1060-6GB, Windows 10 Signature Image - 80VR0078US Like all dedicated gaming laptops, this is a big heavy high-powered machine. It is portable enough to lug over to your buddy's house for play dates, but it is too bulky and heavy to carry to work everyday. Construction is very good with an aggressive-looking aluminum case to match the aggressive-sounding "Legion" product name. Mechanical keyboard has decent (but not the best) travel and the large keys are backlit so you can easily play your games in the dark. Dolby Atmos audio works well for games, but is kind of thin for music or movies unless you hook it up to external speakers. This Y720 version has a 1080p IPS display, which is OK but not as bright or contrasty as some other laptops I have used. There is also a more expensive 4K display available, but I have not tried that.

Core i7 CPU with 16GB of RAm gives you really great performance. This machine is easily powerful enough for any games I tried on it. Even though performance is throttled somewhat when run off the battery, battery life is still less than 2 hours under heavy use (maybe 6 hours with light use).

For the money, it is hard to go wrong with these Lenovo Legions. If you don't want to spend more than $1000, the cheaper Legion Y520 is almost as good for most types of games and costs $300 less.

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR Cable Modem CM500 - Compatible with all Cable Providers incl. Xfinity, Spectrum, Cox | For Cable Plans up to 400Mbps | DOCSIS 3.0 Comcast has repeatedly lied to me, sending me letters and alerts telling me that I need a new cable modem or my service will be seriously degraded. One time they went so far as to set a date when my service would NO longer work at all! Of course, I would never believe them without double-checking for myself, and I found out it was indeed an outright lie. Even the oldest DOCSIS versions can handle more than my 30Mbps connection. I suppose the lie was because they want me to rent their modem for $10 or more a month and relinquish control of my own network to them.

That said, it makes sense to upgrade when convenient to be sure you're future proofed. Eventually even the cheapest Internet plans will be upgraded to higher speeds. When I heard that I could register this on Comcast's network online without having to call them (and have them speak extremely condescendingly to me even though I'm a Systems Engineer), I was sold. Worth doing.

Note that just because DOCSIS 3.0 can reach speeds of 10Gbps with maxed out number of channels, this modem is 680Mbps, which will be out of date eventually, when we finally get Gigabit Ethernet to residences.

Another (of a million) thing(s) I hate about Comcast is that they by default use your AP (that they rent to you as part of a router/AP/modem combo) to create a public (virtual) wireless AP for their other customers. They say this will not affect your bandwidth, but it can affect your throughput. And it uses your electricity. And why would you want to help Comcast, when they take advantage of you any chance they can.

Point of all this is me encouraging you to get your own modem, get your own router and AP (or combo unit, although I prefer them separate) and pare down your ISP bill as much as you can. Stop giving them money.

Note that apparently if you get voice service through Comcast, you'll still need their combo modem unit of some sort. Well, cut that service from your monthly budget too. If we just had some competition, I'd cut Comcast out of my life completely.

Another thing is that if you have their modem and you need help with it, they may call it your responsibility and charge you for any "help" they provide. At least if you own your own stuff, you'll know if it's your problem or theirs.

Modem is straightforward and easy to use as any. If you ever download at high rates for days on end, it'll need cycled, but that's not the modem's fault; it just happens.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Cable Modem CM500 - Compatible with all Cable Providers incl. Xfinity, Spectrum, Cox | For Cable Plans up to 400Mbps | DOCSIS 3.0

text_fidelity_a:
SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro) I began researching these based on reviewing another popular brand. I am a stickler for detail and after hours of research and asking questions I decided to give these a try because of the cost and positive reviews. I bought these for my elderly parent (90 years old) who has hearing loss but does not wear a hearing aid.
After a couple weeks of use I can honestly say these things are great! Very easy to install, easy to use for an elderly person not technically savvy, works from a long distance (we tried the next room), and the volume of these units can go very loud which is good for all types of hearing. There is also a balance control in case a person hears differently in both ears, and a switch to change from normal to higher or lower frequencies to help those with that type of hearing loss.
We can now watch TV when visiting my parent without the TV being so loud. But it is hard to verbally communicate with each other when they wear the headphones, but that’s not a big deal.
You can turn down the TV as low as needed, even muted, but the headphones can be as loud as needed. We used the RCA output from their TV (a 4 year old flat screen) and that works great. We tried it on a new flat screen and worked well also (digital output). All cables are provided along with extra ear inserts.
I like the fact this uses 2.4GHz instead of Bluetooth or infrared which often can lose connection with interference or movement away from the base station. I went out of the room into the next room and heard this one just fine.
The weight was a concern for me but my parent only watches TV for no more than 2 hours at the time and they said it was fine. There are ear loops provided to help with holding the unit if needed.
The only issue I found was that the input on the base station to charge the headphones was oriented backwards to how a person takes off the headset (have to turn the headset around to charge). And when putting on from the base station you have to turn the headphones around else you’ll put it on backwards which is not a big deal, but the volume button and balance will be reversed meaning my parent the first time turned the balance thinking it was volume and thought something was wrong. That’s one more thing for an elderly person to remember, plus you don’t need a lot of pressure to bend/break the charging prongs in the base unit if installed the wrong way.
We used the “speaker” option one time and it worked pretty well to allow a person to hear conversations in the room.

I’ll update this review should something change, but for now I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro)

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Fortunately I bought this at a much cheaper price at $16 instead of the current price as of this writing at $27. There are lots of comparable wireless vertical ergonomic mice less than $27 that also include recharging and cool LED lights. Although it's a decent ergonomic vertical mouse, there are some legitimate gripes with this mouse after months of use so now I'm looking to try a different brand of vertical mouse.

The 2.4Ghz range is pretty bad. I found this out later down the road when I had to switch the USB dongle to a port on the back of my computer. At first I thought my batteries were low (or some dirt interfering with optical sensor) because my mouse cursor would stagger on and off as a moved cursor across screen. That was really frustrating not only for browsing but games. When I put the dongle closer to the front of computer it worked much better.

Now onto the batteries. This may be good or bad depending on preference but it uses AAA batteries. Although replacing batteries seems like an inconvenience, if you have a mouse with a built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery and the batteries go bad or defective then you would have to trash the whole mouse instead of just replacing the batteries.

There is a separate top button on the mouse for DPI toggle (800/1200/1600) but I can't tell what mode it is in unless I move the mouse across the screen every time I toggle it so it is kind of inconvenient. Would be nice so you can visually see the dpi on the mouse or on screen.

Overall, the mouse feel good upon touching it. The texture on the mouse is not glossy plastic but has a slight comfy texture on it. My personal gripe with the ergonomics is it feels a bit narrow and the hand does not feel relaxed. I think the culprit is the thumb rest position feels like it is a bit upwards causes your thumb to squeeze inward instead of relaxing. So I try not to point or put my thumb in the default thumb rest but more below the thumb rest or even slight bend my thumb so it's not straight and stiff.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Mediasonic ProBox HF2-SU3S2 4 Bay 3.5” SATA HDD Enclosure – USB 3.0 & eSATA Support SATA 3 6.0Gbps HDD transfer speed I have had this unit for about four years now. Never a problem. I use it for storing media files and my digital Paintings. It was used for four years on a MacPro 3,1, connected via USB 2. Upgraded the drives over the years, so now it has two 4TB and two 2TB Seagate HDDs.
I just purchased a new (to me) MacPro Trash Can, so I will try the USB 3.
This enclosure is heavy, and not bad looking. The plastic faceplate comes off easy (as it was probably designed to do, to allow easy changing the Hard Drives). But again chances are once you get the drives installed and settings just so, you will not be messing with the door/faceplate. it has tow plastic pins on the bottom and a "latch (Spring loaded)" press and it pops off or on.
The power cord goes in the side, which is weird but not a deal breaker. And unusual configuration, but it is pretty solid and really I don't really mess with it very oftern).
Three fan settings and yes two of them are not quiet. I leave mine on auto and unless I am working on a hot day, moving or writing tons of files, don't hear the fan at all).
The LED lights are not an issue for me, but I could see where in a dark room it would bother some folks. (electrical tape if it really errkks you).
Getting the settings the way you want them takes some trial and error, but once you have them you will most likely not mess with them again.
Drives are easy to add or remove, a couple screws, slide it in the slot.
I have found that if the drive has been formatted and contains data when you add it, you have to force mount it, but once that is done no issues.
So if possible initialize the drive in the enclosure.
This is ideal for novice of mid-level tech geeks, or folks who have a large media collection (Music, movies, photos, etc).
I have hooked it up directly to my Mac Pro and my Wireless router (Orbi) so anyone authorized to access the network can access the media files on it. So my Photos on one drive, Movies on two drives and music on the last drive.
I would highly recommend this to anyone wanting to create a media server.
It DOES NOT have RAID built-in, it can be added via software, but, for a few bucks more you can get the RAID version of this.
text_fidelity_b: Mediasonic ProBox HF2-SU3S2 4 Bay 3.5” SATA HDD Enclosure – USB 3.0 & eSATA Support SATA 3 6.0Gbps HDD transfer speed

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) The Fire HD 10 tablet is pretty much an unbeatable deal for a tablet these days. You get a really good display and decent processor and memory for a great price---especially when it's on sale. And the Fire OS (a rebranded and modified version of Android) works smoothly.

A trade-off is a not-so-good camera resolution.

And there are some limitations on what you can do. If you already own some Android apps, you might not find them in the Amazon app store, and those you do will not credited as paid for. You'll have to buy them again (if you choose to buy).

One option is to follow online instructions for installing the Google Play Store on your Fire. But that's kind of iffy. You don't know when the next Fire OS update might break that installation. And Play Store might download updates to some of the core Fire OS apps that might conflict with proprietary Fire OS modifications.

Another consideration is that this device serves as an advertising and sales platform for Amazon. It's tailored for that. Something to keep in mind.

The thing to consider is if you can be happy with what Amazon gives you. If you're going to be trying to root and work around the OS and app store limitations soon after you get it, maybe it's worth just getting an Android tablet and foregoing the Fire.

If you can be happy with all that, overall it's a great deal for a capable tablet.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

Canon PowerShot SD1100IS 8MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Blue) (OLD MODEL) This is a solid little camera that can provide excellent image quality under the right conditions. But it has two glaring deficiencies:

1. No fill flash option in auto mode. (There is a fill flash option in manual mode, but it's not easy for the casual user to find.) There's red-eye reduction, of course, and you can turn the flash off completely or let the camera decide when to fire it. But with the camera in auto mode, you can't tell it to fire the flash on every shot, regardless of what its sensor thinks. Major bummer when you want to photograph a backlit subject.

2. Shot-to-shot time is agonizingly slow, and focus time isn't especially speedy, either. This is a problem when, for example, you want to catch quick snaps of the animals you see on Disney World's Kilimanjaro Safaris. Ask me how I know.

I'm sure this is a fine camera for people who want to photograph landscapes, still lifes, and posed portraits. For candid shots of subjects in motion, it's not so great.

I generally only keep the two best ones. I tested this one out against my previous champion, which was just a single heavy duty rabbit ear on a magnetic base that somehow beat bigger, newer, and powered models.

The first thing I did with this when I got it was take it apart. I've gotten some in the past where the big plastic dish parts were just plastic for show and had nothing in them. Inside this one were multiple omnidirectional antennas and a circuit board. After attaching it to the coax, I checked through my channels and noticed I was missing some. I then added in the powered section, but didn't turn it on. This totally switched which channels I was missing. Then I turned it on and I got all my channels, plus another one I hadn't previously gotten, so it wins. The various parts do actually do something.

The pictures don't give much idea of scale. It's about the size of a steering wheel and comes with mounting plate. It's kind of huge and I wasn't pleased when I saw the size, but hey, I'll take the size if I get a brand new channel out of the deal.

I received a sample for review but the opinions are my own.

text_fidelity_a:
Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27 We can not find the remote for our Roku or downstairs TV which is a Samsung since we had to remodel over a long period of time due to a flood which started it all. I thought this would be perfect.

BUTTONS
The layout and buttons of this remote are pretty small. They are not difficult to use, however. The explanation in the instructions is pretty good.

USING WITH SAMSUNG AND ROKU
I have an older Samsung TV and a Roku Premiere hooked up to it. At first this worked fine with the TV, but the Roku it just would not work. Finally, I hit the SET UP button and held it until it blinked. I used the S button (next to the TV button) and suddenly instead of having to program the Roku, it just started to work. I did not have to enter roku codes at all.

DOES IT WORK WITH BOTH WELL?
Both of those things work well. I might try to set up DVD later, but for now, all I really wanted was to have the Roku and TV to work. I have a separate satellite remote that I use for DISH so I am not that interested in using this for that as it is upstairs. I would love a Sleep button like my other Samsung remote has, but really that is not a big deal for this particular TV.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For me, once I put in the two AAA batteries, this remote took almost no time to set up for my older Samsung TV and Roku Premiere.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I wish this had a sleep setting to it, but that is minor. It does what I want it to and runs both Roku and Samsung TV nicely.
text_fidelity_b: Philips Universal Remote Control for Samsung, Vizio, LG, Sony, Sharp, Roku, Apple TV, TCL, Panasonic, Smart TVs, Streaming Players, Blu-ray, DVD, 4 Device, Walnut, SRP4320W/27

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic DMC-LX3 10.1MP Digital Camera with 24mm Wide Angle MEGA Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Black) The wide angle lens is wonderful. The field of view and the speed (light gathering ability) of the lens can only be rivaled by high end camera and lens combinations costing six to ten times as much (admittedly those are superior in many other ways as well). Still, the point is that no other compact point and shoot camera can rival the field of view and speed of this one. Nevertheless, some things come up short of fair on the LX3.

The shutter lag is terrible. I am a very instinctive shooter that is quite capable in photojournalist style candids but I am almost always defeated by this camera.

I am not a photophile or electronic gadget spec sheet bench racer. I've done wonderful 8x10 prints with a 6MP camera and 10MP is enough to get prints after substantial cropping. I have huge film scans when I need them but I cannot realistically show dozens of megapixels on screen or in print for more than a handful of images. I also shoot in .jpg and it's great. I can't imagine the agony of terabytes of raw data jamming my PC.

I love the LX3 video quality for movies. It's ideal for Youtube and even Youtube HD. I do not like the Quicktime .MOV format or the weak compression algorithm. I wish it had H.264 and wrote an .MPG type format. It still beats the data format from a DVD camcorder though.

The audio quality for movies is terrible. Again, I'm not talking audiophile critique here. For comparison, my Sony DSC T9 (ultra compact point and shoot) has far better sound.

I hate the manual aspect ratio slider. If I shoot movies I want 16:9 but for stills I want 3:2 (of course). The LX3 requires that I remember to both turn the dial and slide the switch or I will end up shooting 16:9 stills.

Overall, it's a great camera. I hope they get the rest sorted out by the time I expect to buy another one in about 3 or 4 years.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic DMC-LX3 10.1MP Digital Camera with 24mm Wide Angle MEGA Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502 There are so many good reviews here about this antenna, I'll try not to repeat what others have said. I do have a few tips to add,

When setting up your antenna, do yourself a favor and tie a string through the two holes at the top of the antenna. That way you can hang it on one tack/nail as you're searching for the best location. Have extra tacks or nails handy, as they will jump out of your hand and become lost in the carpet (until you find them the next day with a bare foot).

Buy some very small nails. I've discovered that I need to move the antenna around to get reception for some channels. Therefore I have a fair number of nails in the wall that look a little strange. Small nails are less visually distracting. If I get very ambitious, I might even paint them.

This antenna really works best on an exterior wall facing the majority of transmitting antennas you are trying to reach. So if you're working with an interior wall facing the wrong direction, it probably won't work very well.

To up the number of channels you receive, consider buying a signal amplifier (I bought the RCA Digital Amplifier here on Amazon.) They cost about $15. I added 10 additional channels by using one.

Finally, how well these indoor antennas work largely depends on where you live and how close you are to the transmitting antennas. To avoid disappointment, do some research online before purchasing anything.The site that helped me the most was disablemycable.com .
text_fidelity_b: Mohu Television Antenna Leaf 30 Paper-Thin Indoor HDTV Antenna for Free TV MH-110502

Imagine that a huge number of the most popular proper names in existence--names like Target, Macy's, and McDonald's--were completely missing.

Now imagine you had just bought this Garmin, only to discover that this device is, in fact, THAT device.

Don't buy this device. I don't know whether Garmin makes money off of national chains by charging them for inclusion, or what their back-end business model may be, but I was astounded at the number of locations--on this device which had just connected to my computer to download the very latest set of maps--which were missing. If I need to know the address of Target before I can get the Garmin to show me how to get there, I don't need the Garmin.

text_fidelity_a:
Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Hi!

I was very excited about this camera, having used the GoPro exclusively until now.

However, I have to say that I was extremely disappointed with the camera, the website support, the smartphone apps, and the PC software.

I found the camera manual extremely short on important info, such as what I could and could not do while the camera was attached to my computer via the USB cable. There are no instructions anywhere (that I could find) for using the Connect app. I guess they figure people will just touch the screen in various places to see what happens. I was surprised to find that I could record from the Connect app, as info online said that all I could to was "frame" camera shots.

In addition, the camera itself did not work well. The Storyteller software did download and install the latest firmware. Here are some of the things I encountered:

1. The camera would "hang" regularly, as in every time I used it. The only way to "reset" was to remove and replace the battery.

2. Bluetooth communication only worked about 50% of the time, using iPad, iPhone, and iPod.

3. I often had to "reset" the camera (battery re-install) for it to be recognized using the USB connection.

4. Record OFTEN didn't work!! I tried to demo the camera to several people and it would not record unless I re-installed the battery.

5. The camera often would not STOP recording! I would slide back the record switch and the RECORD light would remain on under it and on the bottom of the camera. Again, the only resolution was a battery re-install.

I could find no help for ANY of these issues on the website. I am VERY frustrated by the fact that they do not offer telephone support.

The Storyteller software is terrible, and very lacking in support. It is necessary to eject the camera every time its configuration is reset! This is very frustrating when the camera was only recognized by my computer on a seemingly random basis (I tried all my USB ports and even a different cable!).

I like many things about the Contour much better than the GoPro. However, GoPro has the industry momentum, and if Contour wants to slow that down and gain some traction of its own, their product will need to work better and be much better supported. I think the Contour is a better camera, but the few problems I had with the GoPro were resolved quickly and easily with the information they provided.

I hope this product gets better. Until it - and the support - improves, I can't use it or recommend it to anyone else! :)

hb

UPDATE: Received a call from Contour Tech Support. They "schooled" me on the fact that everything taking place in this camera requires the SD card. There isn't even a little on-board memory. Thus, if the SD card doesn't work exactly right, neither will the camera. Without an SD card working perfectly, all you have is a piece of hardware! They suggested that I format the SD card with the utility at [...] (SD Formatter), and then re-format in the camera. I have already sent back the camera, though!
text_fidelity_b: Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

It looks and feels cheap when compared to others, with the magnetic mesh filters moving out alignment whenever the case is even slightly moved (these also bent quite easily btw), and 3 of the screws that hold the clear acrylic side lost their thread and were loose ever since.

Mine was pretty loud with the 5 fans I put in to help with temperatures. I knew that heat at some level hurt performance, but I had no clue how much my own rig was being crippled by it until I got a new, different case. I've been able to significantly move up my graphics settings in Witcher 3, Battlefield V, and Shadow of The Tomb Raider, and my framerates are still higher and more stable than they used to be when I was using this case. The fact that it feels more as if I upgraded my gpu after moving on from the Q300L shows how much of a drag the temperatures in this case are to gaming performance (I have a 1070 Ti). I had heard about it from tech youtubers and critic reviews but refused to believe it could be this bad until having another case myself and seeing the difference. There are much better cases out there in terms of airflow, it's not worth having this one reduce the performance of your components so much if you're a gamer

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H Though I received this Acer Chromebook for review, I have another one exactly like it that I bought refurbished about a month ago and have been using it a lot. They are both the same make and model. What I like:

1. The battery life is exceptionally long. I can get a long play list going and it will run all night with nearly a full battery in the morning. I'm using Bluetooth earbuds and I darken the screen so I'm sure that helps to save on battery power.
2. Connects quickly with all my Bluetooth earbuds (and I have several). Only one set of earbuds won't connect and I am still trying to figure that out.
3. Boots up quickly - very short wait time.
4. Screen is nice and big and easy to see.
5. Touchpad works great.
6. Keyboard feels good to use and I'm a very fast typer.
7. It was easy to get it started and on-line right out of the box. It didn't ask me for a billion passwords.

What could be better:
1. Sound is rather weak and really not very good.
2. Screen quality (color, brightness, clarity, etc....) is average
3. Seems to be kind of slow going from site to site....my desktops are much faster.
4. It seems this Acer chromebook doesn't send a Bluetooth signal (weaker) as far as my old Haier chromebook. If I want to listen to something while in bed I have to move the Acer to the bottom of the stairs so the signal will reach. Never had that problem before.

But, for the price of this chrombook (as of this review it's around $179.00) I think it's an excellent buy. It comes with a power cord (of course) but that's it. It uses the Chrome web browser and all I want it for is to check a few sites, write reviews and cruise Youtube. It would be great for college/high school students and anyone who doesn't mind storing their data in the cloud. My main reason for using Chromebooks is that you don't have to buy anti-virus for them since they can't download any data so working off line is not feasible.

It seems to be constructed well and I'm happy with the refurb, but now hubs can use one to surf the web too.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H

text_fidelity_a:
Bliksem SSD 128GB SATA III 6Gb/s Internal Solid State Drive 2.5″ 7mm(0.28″) 3D NAND TLC Chip Up to 550 Mb/s for Laptop and Pc KD650 (Black 128GB) This is a great CHEAP sata solid state drive. I want to emphasize that this is CHEAP- it is not going to be a speed demon, and it's not large enough to be a main storage drive to house mission-critical data. But it seems to deliver consistently over 400mbps in benchmark tests, which is more than enough to get the benefits of it over a mechanical drive in a SATA setup.
I can't vouch for the longevity of a brand I've never heard of, but again... the value here is the insanely low price of entry. That makes it great for refurbishing an old laptop or perhaps turning older hardware into a chrome book or a closet file server at home. I like to use it in HDMI recording devices such as an Atmos Ninja, as I can edit footage directly off the drive (it's fast enough!) when plugged into my computer, and it's nice to have a backup from my camera's SD card slot when recording events. If the drive dies one day, nothing major will have been lost. For what it is, so far I am impressed, just have realistic expectations for what you can use it for. I probably would not use this for my main computer C drive if only because it is a laughably small amount of storage. But as a fast SSD that uses legacy SATA connections, it definitely has uses!
text_fidelity_b: Bliksem SSD 128GB SATA III 6Gb/s Internal Solid State Drive 2.5″ 7mm(0.28″) 3D NAND TLC Chip Up to 550 Mb/s for Laptop and Pc KD650 (Black 128GB)

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Standing Leather Case, Fuchsia (will not fit HDX models) This case fits very well and was designed specifically for the Kindle Fire HD 8.9"—with even slick cutouts for the speakers in the back. The Fire just pops right into it and it couldn't be neater or slimmer. The magnetic closure is tidy and holds the case closed quite well. I think Amazon must be trying to recoup some from its bargain-level pricing of its Kindles, however, because I think it's over-priced for what it is (at least at the time of this writing). Still, you can't beat the fit of it.

But a caution is in order for the leather lovers: This may be "genuine leather" but it sure doesn't look or feel like it. If you get it in black or the Saddle Tan, maybe, but the one I was given to review (fuschia) just looks like fancy plastic to me. It has a pebbly texture that makes it easy to hold, but if you want that rich, satisfying feel of well-worn wallet leather, you won't get it with this case. (The Verso Prologue cases have that feel.)

As with so many of the Kindle cases on the market, the inability to clip a stylus to the case is I think an omission. I have a rooCase for my Kindle Fire 7" that I like specifically because I can clip my stylus to the pocket that holds the Kindle. Maybe some hot new designer will come up with a way to design a very slim case that can stow a stylus.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Standing Leather Case, Fuchsia (will not fit HDX models)

text_fidelity_a:
Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI) This wireless range extender was fairly easy to install. The directions were straight forward, and the device was up and running in less than fifteen minutes. It comes with an CD, but we didn't have to use it. We did have to reset the IP address on the computer, but that may have a user issue and not related to the device itself.

It took a little while to find the best place to plug the device in based on our home's layout, but we found one that worked. In our house plan, the best place ended up being in the hallway at baseboard level. Fortunately, the device is small and plugs straight into the wall, eliminating any unsightly cords. It would have been nicer to have the device a little more out of the way. We were a little concerned about this thinking it might get kicked or knocked by the kids as they race around and play. That hasn't happened yet, but it is something to take into consideration if you have small children or pets around. We tried placing it in a less open area hoping to protect it a little more, but none of those areas produced a satisfactory result.

It's very easy to tell how much of a signal the device is receiving from the main router. Three bars is full signal, and one is low signal. The signal indicator light is easy to read and is quite bright. Since the device is in our hallway, it acts as a nice night light and would be rather distracting if it were in a bedroom.

The end result: the dead spots are gone. We can use all of our devices in the those areas without having to worry about losing a signal.
text_fidelity_b: Diamond Multimedia 300Mbps 802.11n Wireless Repeater Range Extender with Wireless Access Point and Wireless Bridge Device (WR300NSI)

I put it on the LONGEST setting so it was up high enough.
IT'S PERFECT and that's partly why I chose this one, it was adjustable.

SUPER EASY to put together - you take the little caps off the screws on the platform and then just screw the legs in and really easy to adjust whatever height you need.

STURDY! - No bends in the middle and while my monitor isn't that big or heavy, seems it could withstand something fairly heavy.

LOOKS! - I love how the stand of my monitor just blends in with the modern looking black riser.

HAS VENTILATION HOLES - for those wanting to put their desktop on it, this could be important that it has the holes in it.

BOTTOMLINE: I got it when it was two dollars off, so a total of about $15, but would have gladly paid more because it's perfect for what I wanted.

text_fidelity_a:
42 Inch/106CM Light Reflector 5-in-1 Collapsible Multi-Disc with Bag - Translucent, Silver, Gold, White and Black for Studio Photography Lighting and Outdoor Lighting I ordered the 43 Inch/110 Centimeter Light Reflector. It comes in it's own little zippered bag. The fabric appears to mostly be nylon, so it should wash easily with a damp cloth. The stitching is solid. I didn't know what to expect, but the Light Reflectors are exactly as pictured. My only little gripe is I had to refer to the listing to remember how to fold it to fit back into the pouch. Once you remove it, you have a large disk, silver on one side, black on the other. This has another zipper on the side. Inside the reflector's zipper is a diffuser which you will need to remove from the larger pouch to use. This is where the mounting tab is located. You will need the mounted clip that is available as part of the kit, or you may purchase it separately. That's not all. The large, outer pouch is reversible, so you then reverse the large pouch and you have a gold reflector one one side or a solid white on the opposite side. This is how you have black, white, gold, silver and a diffuser all in one. The diffuser has it's own tap to clip on your tripod, which pokes through from a button hole to mount the entire piece. You will need to make sure it's pulled through if you remove the outer layer of the reflector.

This is a good purchase for the value. I'm a hobbyist, and sometimes take photos of my projects. My problem comes from being a night-shift worker. I live and work at night. I must make my own lighting setup if I want to photograph anything at night, even in my home. It's light weight, and folds to a small circle, so this is also portable. It weighs less than a pair of jeans.

Here's a free tip: Only use the gold if your subject is brown. I don't find the gold reflector so useful. I'm glad it's available, but I doubt it will get much use for me. Also, place the reflector in a way that would mimic the sun's light, and your subject will look more natural. This is where the clips and extension arms from your tripod can come in handy if you are working solo. Of course, you can always enlist the assistance of another for outdoor shoots. Sometimes this is a best option if it's available. In the movies, they tend to show someone holding a reflector with it facing up towards the subject, but that's only because it does look silly holding a big disc over your head. If you hold it, you will need to hold it up over your head, and it will look silly but your photos will not.

It's a good tool to have on hand for any level of photography. I mostly photograph my doll collection. Once or twice a year, our doll collectors group will gather outdoors for shoots. We've not had a reflector available to us before, so this will help us immensely finding good spots to make photographs, even if the clouds are moving or we want to setup under trees.

I also ordered the 2-pack clips. These are nice because they come with an adapter on them. If you remove the threaded black female cylinder and threaded ring, you are left with a standard sized male mount that will fit a tripod base. You do not need to make a separate purchase for an adapter, it's already there. The ball joint swivels all the way around and there is a groove in the base to tilt the clip in towards the base, so you can use these clips for holding the reflectors, diffuser or even a backdrop on a side or top mount adapter of your backdrop frame.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.
text_fidelity_b: 42 Inch/106CM Light Reflector 5-in-1 Collapsible Multi-Disc with Bag - Translucent, Silver, Gold, White and Black for Studio Photography Lighting and Outdoor Lighting

HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA) I got my first PC in 2003, and had a corded mouse. Looking back, I can BARELY remember the mouse that came with that Gateway PC. In 2004, my mom bought a Dell PC and traded me for my Gateway – don’t judge, she just wanted something to browse the internet and play games on.

Between 2003-2005, I used an awkward racecar shaped mouse, but went back to the more streamlined corded mouse for my desktops.

In 2005, when I got a laptop, I got my first wireless mouse and liked it. It was a Logitech.

By 2010, I got my first HP laptop – and as usual, got a specific mouse for it, again Logitech. The reason? My hand. I don’t have very big hands and hate to “splay” my fingers out trying to grip the mouse. That continued with a backup laptop in 2011 with some college money.

I even got “backup” mice, I just LOVED the Logitech ones.

Last year, 2021, I got another HP laptop for my birthday and yes – a “Logi” mouse (M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top). This was a bit smaller than my previous mice. But, I love it.

Thinking this might be a bit better – I got it.

Right off – it is a bit “extra”. I can BARELY grip it to get it to do what I need to do. The “thumb” rest was a good idea, the USB rechargeable feature was nice, programmable buttons – a bit beyond me. This is definitely for someone who needs those features.

As far as “quiet” with regards to the scrolling and clicking – I don’t see the need for the feature. When I’m typing on they keyboard that is noisier than my mouse.

It was response and fast – but not enough to justify a purchase of it.

It connects the same way my “Logi” does – USB dongle. Both mice take ONE (1) AA battery

At the current price of $67.52 – this is a definitely no-go for me.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 010-02172-31 Vivoactive 4S, Smaller-Sized GPS Smartwatch, Features Music, Body Energy Monitoring, Animated Workouts, Pulse Ox Sensors and More, Light Gold with Light Pink Band I have owned this watch for a year and a half now. I use it almost daily for my walks/runs, weight workouts, and indoor bike workouts. The main reason I chose this watch in the first place was because it was one of the smaller ones available. I am 5'9 but have small wrists, and really disliked the 'utilitarian' look of larger watches. After a year and a half, I am so tired of the issues with it and ready to jump ship. If I used this watch more regularly (I only wear it for workouts - not all day), I would have switched a LONG time ago. The amount of people who have complained about the same issues for YEARS without Garmin doing anything makes me hesitant to purchase another Garmin product, especially with the Apple Watch, Samsung, and now Google buying out Fitbit and coming up with a watch.
- Spotify on this watch seriously sucks. If you check Spotify forums, you will find COUNTLESS threads of suggestions for the Spotify app on this watch that should truly be basic features at this price. Do they implement them or listen? No. Also, there is no way to contact Spotify customer service - you just get pointed towards their 'community forum' where you have people complaining of the same exact things with no fix. You can't skip forward on any track, at all. I listen to a lot of podcasts when I walk. Some are 2 hours in length while my walk is only 1 hour. This watch constantly either reverts to the very beginning of my podcast so I have to start all over (because again, you can't skip forward - so have fun listening to ads as well!) in anything, only updates 1 song out of 15 on my playlist or get the error 'sync failed', or some other random issue. Also, if you have a playlist on Spotify, you cannot choose the track you want to listen to. You have to hit the >> button to get to where you want. Really? I hope Garmin drops Spotify because they have been a truly horrible app on this watch the entire time with no effort to make updates. Take a look at the reviews of Spotify on the Garmin store if you don't believe me.
- Battery life is a couple of days. However, there are points in time where my watch will be at say 80% the night before, I get ready to leave and go my walk the next morning, pick up my watch, and it's at 8%. WTF? This happens enough to be super annoying and apparently is not an 'only me' problem. It appears to be tied to when the watch updates.
- I tried to wear this to track my sleep in the beginning and gave up after two nights due to the extreme disco effect of the 'gesture' motions. I tried turning on the 'do not disturb' function advertised on the watch which is supposed to disable this stupidly bright light that WILL wake you and whoever is next to you up. Didn't work. Do a search for 'Garmin watch lights up in middle of the night' and you will find all sorts of people complaining of the same thing, and not just on this version of the watch.
- GPS has issues connecting and can take several minutes which is pretty annoying when you try to start tracking an activity only to see a red bar when trying to connect. I 'sync' my watch to my phone constantly so that is not the issue. I have switched between the GPS options Garmin offers on the watch to no avail. Search for this issue as well and you will see lots of people with the same complaint.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-02172-31 Vivoactive 4S, Smaller-Sized GPS Smartwatch, Features Music, Body Energy Monitoring, Animated Workouts, Pulse Ox Sensors and More, Light Gold with Light Pink Band

Samsung 860 QVO SSD 4TB - 2.5 Inch SATA 3 Internal Solid State Drive with V-NAND Technology (MZ-76Q4T0B/AM), Gray I’ve had this SSD for a few days and I also have a 1TB 970 Evo Plus and 1TB 860 Evo and all of them are great! But they do have their drawbacks too.

This drive does really well with SMALL (under 15Gb) workloads. The speeds are right up there (~500MB/s R/W) with my 860 Evo until it gets to about ~14GB at which point it slows down drastically. This is fine for things like boot, games, apps, and most programs.

However, if you do heavy workloads like video editing, file transfers, etc,. where you are regularly moving large (15GB+) files around this is NOT the drive for you. If you are a “heavy” user I highly recommend the 860 Pro. It can keep up those high R/W speeds without slowing down after ~15GB. It will maintain full speed throughout the duration of whatever you are doing.

With that said this is a great drive for light/moderate workloads (gaming, web browsing, small work files, etc.,) and it is at a price that gives you excellent value and quality for your money.

I also really love the Samsung Magician software. It’s basically the main reason why 3/5 of my drives are Samsung. Samsung is also known for making reliable, high quality products. Yes there is a premium compared to cheaper drives but you’re paying that little bit extra for quality & reliability.

I took off 1 Star on this review though because Samsung doesn’t include any of the cables or mounting screws which just doesn’t make sense to me. C’mon Samsung start adding that stuff! I would’ve happily paid a couple dollars more for it and it wouldn’t have cost Samsung that much so they could’ve made a little bit of extra profit by adding it.

I still recommend this drive though and would buy it or the 860 Evo again if I needed more storage.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 860 QVO SSD 4TB - 2.5 Inch SATA 3 Internal Solid State Drive with V-NAND Technology (MZ-76Q4T0B/AM), Gray

So far, with the wrapping ear piece, this pair seems to stay on my ears much better than the buds that just pop into the ears. They paired easily to my iPhone and connect automatically each time I take them out of the case. The sound is decent or at least decent enough for me. I do not use these for just listening to music or videos, I have better over the ear headphones for that purpose. For me, I just use these for running, working out or maybe while working around the yard. For that purpose, the sound quality is pretty good. The only suggestion I have is remember to take the clear tape off the charging contacts; I did not realize it was there and my earbuds were not charging each time I put them back in the case. On the upside, I did learn that the battery life is excellent on these earbuds. I cannot say how long they actually lasted before I charged them, but I probably went on 5 or 6 runs before the first ear bud died. With the tape off the contacts, they do charge automatically each time they are placed back in their case. A nice feature is that the case can be charged either with a cord or by setting the case on a charging pad. The price was reasonable. I would recommend these wireless earbuds to anyone looking for a set. Since I cannot fully say how long they will last or how durable they are, I will reserve the 5th star until I have owned these for a while.

Updated 12May21: Ok, I really want to like earbuds, but I cannot. As many times as I have tried earbuds, they just always feel like they are coming out of my ears, even w/the ear wraps on these buds. Having to continuously re-seat the ear buds in my ears while running just doesn't make for a comfortable run. So, I went back to a pair of wired BT headphones; which sit in my ears much better.

But the future upgradability seemed like it'd be very costly. Over all, this chip performs just fine. I mainly upgraded so I could play Diablo 3, and with an EVGA 550 Ti, I play it on high settings, and it looks as good as I could want it to look. My old machine did just fine with standard productivity stuff, but I wanted to play games that were more recent than WoW. I'm able to do everything I want, with no signs of a lag. If I need to upgrade, I'm banking that the next generation of this chip will see some improvements (though the improvement I'm seeing from my last CPU is leaps-and bounds!) The AM3+ socket will be around for a while. Over all, this is a great chip, and easy on the wallet.

**Update 9/6/12**
I recently purchased Guild Wars 2. The game is fairly CPU-intensive, but the FX-4100 keeps up just fine! I think I'm sitting at around 50% plus load at any given time during actual game play on all four cores. I haven't had a single hiccup or spot of lag yet!

Starcraft 2 is another CPU-heavy application, and coupled with the 550 Ti card, I'm running it on Extreme at 1400x900 resolution, and it's flawless. Again, all four cores are loaded, and quite frequently, they're over 60%. Things get a little warm (35C or so) when compared to when I run other applications. Nothing to worry about!

I have also paid quite a bit of attention to how it runs with Diablo 3. It only uses 2 cores at about 50% load at any given time. That game is more GPU-intensive. I am still very happy with my purchase!
text_fidelity_b: AMD FX 4100 4-Core Processor, 3.6 4 Socket AM3+  FD4100WMGUSBX

Regetek 7" Double DIN Touchscreen in Dash Bluetooth Car Stereo Mp3 Audio 1080P Video Player FM Radio/AM Radio/TF/USB/AUX-in + Remote Control I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the cables (both the one from the charger to the control module, and the 3.5mm connection) are hardwired. This means that if either cable becomes damaged it can cost more to repair than to replace, unless you have the skills to repair them. Had the charger been configured with a micro USB port and the control module with a 3.5mm port for separate cables that can be easily purchased just about anywhere (including pharmacies and supermarkets these days), a damaged cable would be an easy swap and the value and utility of this solution been a lot more.

Operationally, this kit functions as promised. The mic will pass through commands if your phone has voice recognition, and the overall quality of sound is more a function of your vehicle's stereo system than this unit. Since my vehicle is already bluetooth-enabled I used a small, powered speaker with a 3.5mm input to test this. Since the cable, as mentioned, is fixed I had to still perform the test in my vehicle. The sound quality was overall good, and making and receiving test calls were easy and the connections clear enough to be heard without 'can you hear me now?'

Surprisingly the extra USB port in the charger was relatively fast, and proved to be as good as any high-speed (but non QC) charger on both my Note 4 and a friend's iPhone 5S. In fact, that is why I only subtracted one star because while the cable issue does detract, the charging capability of the extra port is better than I expected.

Bottom line: this is an OK hand's free solution for older vehicles that have an AUX port, but no bluetooth (and you NEED an AUX port to make this work.) Since the control module is hardwired into a lighter-style charger you cannot use this with a home stereo that does not have bluetooth, but does have 3.5mm input. There are similar solutions that use basically the same design, but replaceable cables that do allow this, so this one is restricted to vehicle-only use. If that is all you need, this one does perform as claimed.
text_fidelity_b: Regetek 7" Double DIN Touchscreen in Dash Bluetooth Car Stereo Mp3 Audio 1080P Video Player FM Radio/AM Radio/TF/USB/AUX-in + Remote Control
